text:
[LLEX.11.3.1] Resolution order for a numeric literal followed by a
non-space token: **`UNIT_LIT` (numeric prefix, an optional `_`, and a
unit suffix — or a numeric prefix directly followed by an angle glyph
`°`/`′`/`″`) → `FLOAT_LIT` scientific (`Ne…`) → error.**

`COMPLEX_LIT` is **not** a rung in v1. It is the surface syntax of the
`complex` type, which is deferred ([LUNI.14]), so a bare `i`/`j` suffix
reaches no token class at all, and `5i` is refused ([LUNI.14.9]).

A digit directly followed by an alphabetic character **is** a unit
literal: `30s`, `100km` and `30x` each lex as one token. The first two
name known units; `30x` names an unknown one and is an unknown-unit
error, never `30 * x` ([LUNI.3.1.4]).

Since the separator is optional it is not what separates these classes.
What does is the suffix restriction of [LUNI.3.1.5]: a bare `i`/`j`, and
an `e`/`E` followed by digits, are withheld from `UNIT_SUFFIX`. That
withholding is the only reason `1e6` reaches `FLOAT_LIT` at all, and —
with `COMPLEX_LIT` absent from v1 — it is why `5i` and `5_i` alike reach
no token class. The separator changes neither: it is
optional, so it cannot be what tells them apart.
